paragraph: Wallington runs on two property types, and they behave differently. Single-family is the larger tier with 13 sales over six months at a median of $745,000, a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00, and a median of 28 days on market. About 31 percent sold above asking. That's competitive but not frenzied. Priced homes are moving, and sellers are generally getting close to what they ask without a bidding war doing the work. The range runs from $570,000 to $1,275,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. Multi-family, by contrast, is the tighter market. Nine sales at a median of $760,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.05, two thirds selling above asking, and a median of 19 days on market. Sellers are dictating terms in that tier, though nine sales is a thin sample and one strong month moves the number. The monthly counts are too small to read a seasonal trend here, so treat the six-month picture as the real read. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and single-household simplicity of a detached home or the rental income and tenant management that comes with a two- or three-family.
